pr_title: Move physical-cpu-count into the monorepo and make it more reliable
pr_body:

issue_context.title: /bin/sh: lscpu: not found on Alpine Linux
issue_context.body:
# 🙋 Feature Request

In order to make the tool more user-friendly it is nice to have separation between:
- error messages, that considerably affect how the tool works (like functionality, performance, etc.);
- warning messages, that just states something that might be useful for someone.

## 😯 Current Behavior

A red-colored message appears in console which states:
`/bin/sh: lscpu: not found`

From user's perspective the message text and color is confusing and forces to investigate it's cause - check other platforms, understand whether there is a fallback for this functionality, ensure the user's application build is made without any issues.

## 💁 Possible Solution

As as user I would be happy to see that it's just a warning that brings some non-critical information.
This may be done by changing the message color to something less shocking (e.g. yellow) and changing the message text to something like:
`/bin/sh: lscpu: not found. "os.cpus" fallback is used instead`


## 🔦 Context

Got this problem while building UI application with docker using Alpine image, e.g.
`FROM node:11-alpine`

## 💻 Examples

Decided to ask you again since there was an opened issue before (#2031) and it is yet not solved.

PS not sure if that's really a feature request or a bug
comments:
I'm not sure where this message is coming from,
https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/6cbf2a65cdcd66af135ff9eca2a3799bde9f8a5b/packages/core/workers/src/cpuCount.js#L3-L11

physical-cpu-count source:
https://unpkg.com/physical-cpu-count@2.0.0/index.js

I agree a warning would be way more user friendly.

Another workaround that hasn't been mentioned here but I'll add it for reference: if you know what the cpu count is on your machine you can set the environment variable `PARCEL_WORKERS` to that amount or just `PARCEL_WORKERS=1` as a safe option. If this is set, then Parcel doesn't try to detect the cpu count itself and it will never attempt to run `lscpu`. [Here it is in the docs.](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/cbbbbbeae42e1d2ea7c8e72f303602771d5858da/CONTRIBUTING.md#environment-variables-command-line-arguments)

Why are you using `lscpu` at all?
`uname -p` will give you the architecture and `nproc` the number of cores
@abramenal this is an issue with the physical cpu count package, I'll move it into the parcel monorepo and open a PR later today, so this error hopefully no longer occurs in Parcel 2.

@DeMoorJasper cool!
Let me know if I can help with anything

Opened the PR, it uses `nproc` first and after that tries `lscpu` so it should work on alpine and in case it fails it does it silently so it does not alarm anyone as it would have no effect, besides maybe a small performance decrease. See #4029

review_comments: This silences the output, so we don't get any errors or warnings in the console from this util

I removed support for windows because the test failed due to timeout which shouldn't happen.

The command windows runs is just too slow not entirely sure if there is a way to even support it without it taking seconds.
